task: Resolve the meaning of the 0x24 comparison in the 2.24 Button-Test parser
hypothesis_tested: Does the immediate 0x24 in _RainbowTestState::analysisData (entry 0x91d130) at instruction 0x91d168 mean a 36-byte frame length, the integer 18 in Smi/tagged form, a container length, an array element index, a byte offset, an enum value, or something else?
verdict: PROVEN STATIC: 0x24 is the Dart Smi (tagged) encoding of the integer 18 (0x12 << 1). It is compared against data[1] - the frame's byte at index 1, the frame length/type field, whose value is 0x12 = 18 for a full 18-byte report frame. It is NOT 36, NOT a 36-byte frame length, NOT an index, NOT a byte offset, NOT an enum value.

LIVE-PINNED 4.0.8 GATE (anchor for the argument encoding):
4.0.8 0x00acfaac: 1f100071 cmp  w0, #4              ; tagged Smi 2 => frame[2] == 2, matches live frame A5 12 02 (byte[2]=0x02)
=> the gate accessor's argument immediate is TAGGED; 2.24's #2 is therefore Smi 1 => index 1.
smi_tagging_chain: 1. Dart Smi n is stored as (n << 1) | 0 (low tag bit 0).
2. List<int> elements in this image are proven tagged (frame builder emits 0x14A for 0xA5, 0xA for 0x05, 0x1A4 for 0xD2, 2 for 0x01, 0xFA for 0x7D; GrowableList length 5 stored as 0xA).
3. w0 at 0x91d168 is the return of a List<int> element accessor -> w0 is a tagged Smi.
5. The tagged form of the integer 36 would be 0x24 << 1 = 0x48, so 36 is arithmetically excluded.
6. 2.22/2.23 compile the same source with an explicit untag and compare against 0x12 = 18 -> source constant is 18.
7. The accessor takes exactly one argument (2 stack slots / pop #0x10, vs the no-arg property getter at 1 slot / pop #8) -> indexed element read, not .length.
8. Argument immediate #2 is tagged -> index 1 -> data[1], the frame byte whose value is 0x12 = 18.

branch_behavior.equal: fall through to 0x91d170: data.sublist(3,14) -> Uint8List.fromList -> asByteData -> (len>3) -> extract 32-bit big-endian mask from bytes [3][4][5][6]
branch_behavior.not_equal: b.ne #0x91e23c -> immediate return (mov x0,NULL; ...; ret); frame discarded

alternative_interpretations.candidate: a 36-byte frame length / the raw integer 36
alternative_interpretations.reason: 36 as a Dart integer is emitted as 0x48, never 0x24; the compared byte is 0x12=18, so ==36 could never pass.
the accessor takes one argument (indexed read), not the no-arg .length property. Numerically the compared element IS the frame's length field, so 18 coincides with the frame size (18 bytes).
the index is the separate immediate mov x16,#2 = Smi 1 (index 1); 0x24 is the compared value.
0x24 is a comparison operand, not used in any address computation.
the operand is a tagged SmallInteger element of a List<int>; no enum dispatch present.

alternative_interpretations.candidate: a tagged integer of another kind (Mint / heap int)
alternative_interpretations.reason: tag bit is 0, value fits a Smi, no AllocateMint stub on this path.
w0 is a tagged Smi; 0x24>>1=0x12=18; 2.22/2.23 untag and compare to 0x12.

residual_uncertainty: The dispatch target of GDT[cid_x0 - 0x30c] is unnamed in the dump; it is inferable only as 'a one-int-argument accessor on List<int>' (operator[]/elementAt). Naming it would require resolving the class id to its method table.
